title: Pavlova
subtitle: Crisp meringue with cream and fresh berries
excerpt: A large meringue with a crisp shell and marshmallow centre, piled with softly whipped cream and fresh summer berries. The showpiece dessert of the Australian and New Zealand kitchen.

recipe.sourceNotes: The pavlova was created in honour of the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova during her tour of Australia and New Zealand in the 1920s, though both countries dispute who invented it first. The defining characteristic that distinguishes pavlova from other meringue desserts is the marshmallow-soft interior: this is achieved by adding cornflour and white wine vinegar to the meringue mixture, which stabilises the egg white foam and prevents it from fully drying out during baking. The outside bakes hard and crisp while the inside remains soft. The pavlova must be assembled just before serving: the cream and fruit soften the crust after about 30 minutes and the marshmallow interior begins to weep. The base can be made up to 24 hours ahead and stored in an airtight tin.

recipeTools.notes: One large baking tray lined with baking parchment.

content.text: The bowl and whisk must be scrupulously clean and free of grease, as even a trace of fat prevents the egg whites from whipping. Separate the eggs cold but whip at room temperature: room-temperature whites whip to a larger volume. Add the sugar a tablespoon at a time once the whites reach stiff peaks: adding it too quickly causes the meringue to weep. The meringue is done when it is stiff, glossy, and holds a firm peak. Draw a 24 cm circle on the parchment as a guide and build the sides slightly higher than the centre to create a bowl for the cream.

items.preparation: halved; flesh and seeds scooped out

content.text: Heat the oven to 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Draw a 24 cm circle on a piece of baking parchment and place on a baking tray. Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks. Add the sugar a tablespoon at a time, whisking well between each addition, until the meringue is thick, glossy, and holds a firm peak.

Fold in the cornflour, vinegar, and vanilla with a large metal spoon. Spoon the meringue onto the parchment circle. Build up the sides slightly higher than the centre to create a slight bowl. Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until crisp outside but still pale ivory in colour. Turn the oven off and leave the meringue inside until completely cold, at least 2 hours or overnight.
Just before serving, whip the cream to soft peaks and spoon over the meringue. Arrange the strawberries and raspberries on top. Drizzle over the passion fruit pulp. Serve immediately.
